vectors.description: A well-formed public root whose fingerprint the caller pinned.
The same root with no pinned fingerprint: accepted as well-formed, reported unpinned.
An unknown field is refused, never dropped: there is no slot for anything but public material.
An unknown field inside the root entry is refused too.
A public key of the wrong length is not admitted.
The identity point verifies any message on the platform primitive: it is never admitted as a root.
A root of an algorithm this verifier does not support is not a root.
A root may authorize keys and nothing else: granting it the checkpoint purpose makes it a signer of checkpoints.
A root is never an attestation signer.
The artifact in hand is not the one whose fingerprint the caller pinned.
After a reset the caller raises the minimum epoch; the older root is refused.
A production verifier refuses any key id that begins with synthetic-.
A version this verifier does not speak is reported, not read.
A bootstrap with no root is refused.
Nothing is bootstrapped from anything else: with no bootstrap there is nothing to verify against.
The root authorizes the first operational key for the checkpoint purpose, generation 1.
A statement that names the root but was signed by another key.
A statement that names a root other than the pinned one is refused before its signature is asked.
The authorized public key edited after signing.
The granted purposes edited after signing.
The generation edited after signing.
The root epoch edited after signing.
The statement signed under the checkpoint domain tag is not an authorization.
The statement signed under an attestation domain tag is not an authorization.
The statement signed as bare JSON, with no domain at all.
An operational key that names itself as the root and signs its own authorization bootstraps nothing: the pinned root is the only root.
A statement that names the real root but was signed by the operational key it authorizes.
The root key may not also be the operational key.
STANDING_HEAD is a reserved purpose: it is not grantable.
No attestation purpose is ever grantable to a governance key.
Purposes are strictly ordered, like every list in the format.
An authorization signed for epoch 2 cannot be replayed under the epoch 1 bootstrap, even by the same key.
A signature that is not 64 bytes of hex.
A signature with its last character changed.
Routine rotation: generation 2 retires the first key through the last state it signed and names the new one.
Generation 3 marks the second key compromised and retains nothing of it.
Generations must be 1..N with nothing missing.
The same generation twice is not an extension.
Generation 2 must name the digest of generation 1.
A later generation that names no predecessor.
Generation 1 has nothing to supersede.
A key once superseded is never authorized again.
The caller holds generation 3; a chain that stops at generation 2 is older state, never current.
The caller holds one generation 2; a chain with a different generation 2 is a fork.
The caller holds generation 2; generation 3 is a successor.
The caller holds generation 3 and has generation 3.
A held state that is not a generation and a digest.
Below the minimum epoch nothing in the chain is evaluated.
A checkpoint by the current operational key: signature valid, signer authorized, reliance granted.
After rotation, a checkpoint by the retired key at a state inside what the root stood behind is still relied upon.
A checkpoint at exactly the retained state, with exactly the retained heads.
A checkpoint by the retired key past what the root retained: the signature is valid and the signer is no longer relied upon. New checkpoints require the new key.
A checkpoint by the retired key at the retained count but over another history: it is not the state the root reviewed.
A checkpoint signed by a key the root marked compromised and retained nothing of: valid signature, no reliance.
After the replacement the new key's checkpoint is relied upon.
A checkpoint by a key the root never authorized.
A checkpoint that names an authorized key id with another key's material authorizes nothing.
With the bootstrap below the epoch floor nothing is relied upon and no trust root is derived.
The caller holds generation 3; a stale chain with only the first key does not relieve the held state.
Under the new root the old lineage's operational key is not authorized: the signature stays valid, the reliance does not.
Under the new root its own operational key is relied upon.
Two distinct origins confirm the same fingerprint: the candidate may be pinned.
One origin is not independent confirmation.
Two confirmations from one origin are one origin: GitHub alone is not an independent trust root.
A confirmation of a different fingerprint does not count, and says so.
No confirmation at all.
A candidate that is not a bootstrap.
A higher epoch, a different root key and two distinct origins: the consumer may re-pin.
A candidate at the pinned epoch is not a reset.
A new epoch that keeps the compromised key is not a reset: root-signed replacement is not recovery.
A new root nobody confirmed out of band.
The root the consumer relies on is described wrongly.
A complete two-person root bootstrap transcript that matches its public artifacts and carries no secret slot.
A transcript with a field the format does not define is refused: it has no free slot.
An event attested by one role only.
An event whose checklist is not complete.
The root digest the transcript records is not the digest of the bootstrap supplied.
A backup recorded below the policy floor.
Events recorded out of order.
A live transcript may not name a synthetic key.
The tooling digests are not the published ones.
With no artifacts supplied the transcript is checked for shape only, and says so.
